comments.text: It will be interesting to see how "attention is all you need" holds up. The ability trigger off an idea from whatever is happening around me allows me to go off on an ADD tangent, to go off into my own little zone/world. You can always come back to the information in the attention zone since it is not so fleeting. Identifying a best approach is part of the process to solving a problem. comments.author: @ScottLahteine
comments.text: A lot of scientific discovery, and certainly hypotheses, can be done as an exercise in refining and improving the precise meaning of tokens, their properties, and their relationships to other tokens, and iterating on those networks to shake out anomalies and hypotheses that don’t align with data. An agent system built on LLMs can likely do this by operating on a collection of LoRAs instead of working directly on large models. To this end, it could be useful to have a network trained purely on facts about natural phenomena with all other trivia removed, to try and build a “core truth network” with a connectome that is fundamental and which can be used as a backbone within larger networks that still include junk and trivia.

comments.author: @DavidSaintloth
comments.text:
Okay, so now that the architecture and approach is out there for others to replicate, it's just a matter of time to see if people get similar traction. 

I am curious to know more about how they define their different modules of an architecture. The paper doesn't delineate or distinguish what these modules are. It just lists them... And arguably there are a lot of them. 

Many are derived from common components. Used in papers today but a whole bunch of them look like hybrids that I've never seen before. 

That said, looking at their high level research and engineering approach, it does replicate exactly the process that researchers and Engineers utilize to create new novel papers. You look at what's out there. You come up with some hypotheses on how to make what out there. Better you test your hypotheses in the context of your papers. Methodology you compare your results against out there and you repeat the cycle. 

Automating this in an efficiency manner alone, it returns significant results as you could set this as an agent to just go work. You could have it focus on specific areas in research so that it could rather than generalize Solutions create Solutions which are novel in a specific subdomain.
